Week 2 Executive Summary

Week 2 of the Rodent Eradication Program at the Rehabilitation Center of Orlando has produced exceptional results. The program continues to perform ahead of its projected target timeline, and the substantial reduction in active rodent population within the facility is a direct reflection of the effectiveness of the treatment strategy combined with the outstanding cooperation of your maintenance team and dietary staff.

Week 2 Status: Exceptional Progress — Ahead of Schedule. Pest Pro service personnel located and removed a total of 9 rodents during Week 2 service visits. In addition, facility maintenance staff independently located and removed 2 rodents — one juvenile and one large adult — demonstrating the effectiveness of the coordinated effort between Pest Pro and your team. Evidence of additional rodent casualties was also observed that could not be fully located or retrieved. Most significantly, dietary staff have reported a complete decline in observed rodent activity during Week 2 — no sightings or sounds of activity were reported by kitchen personnel throughout the entire service period.

Week 2 Activities and Observations

Services were conducted on an every-other-day schedule during Week 2 (four visits), as outlined in the original service agreement. The following activities and conditions were observed and addressed during this reporting period.

  • Rodent Removal — Pest Pro: A total of 9 rodents were located and removed by Pest Pro service personnel during Week 2 visits. All mechanical traps, glue boards, and monitoring stations were checked, reset, and rebaited at each service visit.
  • Rodent Removal — Maintenance Staff: Facility maintenance staff located and removed 2 additional rodents independently during Week 2 — one juvenile and one large adult. This level of staff engagement is commended and reflects the coordinated commitment to resolving this infestation.
  • Additional Casualties: Evidence of additional rodent casualties was observed in several locations throughout the facility. Not all casualties could be fully located or retrieved due to access limitations within void spaces and mechanical areas.
  • Dietary Staff Report: Dietary staff reported a complete cessation of observed rodent activity during Week 2. No sightings and no audible signs of rodent movement were reported by kitchen personnel throughout the entire service period — a significant and encouraging milestone.
  • Structural Penetration Sealing: The majority of interior and perimeter penetration points identified during the initial assessment have now been sealed. Exclusion materials including galvanized steel mesh, commercial-grade foam sealant, and wire-reinforced barriers have been applied at priority access points throughout the facility.
  • Exterior Conditions: While meaningful progress has been made on the building exterior, several areas of concern remain. Continued attention to exterior vegetation, ground-level harborage areas, and perimeter conditions is necessary and must remain an active priority for the maintenance team.
  • Above-Ceiling — Dietary HVAC Ducting: Remediation work on damaged HVAC ductwork above the drop ceiling in the dietary area is actively underway. This remains one of the most critical structural access points identified during the program and must be brought to full completion.

Exterior Conditions — Areas of Ongoing Concern

Although improvement has been observed along portions of the building exterior, a number of conditions remain that require continued attention. While the interior program has produced substantial results, sustained pressure from the exterior will limit the long-term effectiveness of the eradication effort if these items are not fully resolved.

Note: The exterior perimeter of the facility, while improved, still presents areas of concern. Vegetation management, ground-level harborage conditions, and remaining structural gaps along the exterior must continue to be addressed by the maintenance team throughout the duration of this program. These items are directly linked to the ongoing exterior rodent pressure on the building and to the program's ability to achieve and maintain full control.

Program Schedule and Billing Summary

Based on the substantial reduction in rodent activity observed during Week 2 — including the complete cessation of activity reported by dietary staff — Pest Pro is adjusting the Week 3 service frequency from every-other-day to three times per week. This adjustment reflects the meaningful progress achieved and represents the next appropriate step in the program's transition toward full control.

Week 2 Photo Documentation

The following photographs were taken by Pest Pro service personnel during Week 2 service visits. They document penetration points that have been sealed as part of the ongoing exclusion effort, as well as a representative rodent retrieval from this reporting period.

Photo 1 — Interior Penetration Point: Sealed. Previously open wall penetration at floor level surrounding a utility assembly — a confirmed rodent entry and travel point. Commercial-grade sealant and barrier material have been applied to close the gap and prevent further passage through the wall void.
Photo 2 — Mechanical Room Penetration: Sealed. Open void space behind mechanical equipment in the facility's pump and HVAC room — a confirmed rodent harborage and travel corridor. Exclusion product has been applied into the equipment void to close the penetration point and eliminate this access route.
Photo 3 — Dietary Kitchen Penetration: Sealed. Galvanized steel hardware cloth and commercial sealant installed at the base of a kitchen equipment column, closing a confirmed rodent entry point at the floor-to-wall junction within the primary active zone of the dietary kitchen.
Photo 4 — Retrieved Rodent: Week 2. Representative photograph of a rodent retrieved during Week 2 service operations. The condition and location of retrieval are consistent with mortality resulting from the active treatment program. A total of 9 rodents were located and removed by Pest Pro during this reporting period, with additional casualties identified but not fully retrievable from within structural void spaces.

Looking Ahead — Week 3

Pest Pro will begin its three-times-per-week service schedule for Week 3 on March 27, 2026. Service visits will continue to focus on the dietary kitchen and all associated access areas, above-ceiling spaces, mechanical rooms, and the building perimeter. All monitoring devices will be checked and serviced at each visit, and any remaining open penetration points will be addressed in coordination with maintenance staff.

A Week 3 progress report will be issued upon completion of the service period and will include an updated status on all pending items, capture and retrieval data, and the recommended service frequency for Week 4.

The progress achieved during Weeks 1 and 2 reflects the exceptional coordination between Pest Pro and the staff at the Rehabilitation Center of Orlando. We remain fully committed to delivering a complete and lasting resolution to this infestation.
